identity.name: Ariel Ruth Marin
identity.headline: Multilingual AI training & quality lead · applied linguist
identity.summary: Applied linguist running quality for multilingual AI training data at scale: 200–300 annotators across 10–12 languages, producing around 500,000 annotations a week. I built the multilingual programme they work inside — the training, certification and audit layers that hold output consistent as client guidelines move — and quality scores have risen since. Before AI, six years of linguistic quality control in regulated medical translation, and four years teaching and designing curricula across three countries.

experience.title: Training Quality Manager — Multilingual Human Data Annotation

highlights.text: Own training and certification for 200–300 crowd-sourced annotators working across 10–12 languages, built directly from client project-initiation documentation.
Hold output consistent at around 500,000 annotations a week as client guidelines shift, through living documentation and targeted retraining.
Run initial training, shadow sessions, audits and audits-of-audits across the programme, surfacing quality trends and clearing blockers before they reach production data.
Report quality and performance daily, weekly and monthly against the client's taxonomy; quality scores have improved over the period under this reporting.

experience.title: Training & Quality Manager — English to Multilingual Expansion

highlights.text: Stood up five multilingual workflows from existing English client documentation, establishing the monitoring, shadowing and audit processes that carried each from first training to production data.
Extended the programme into six additional languages — eleven in total — replicating the process and adapting it to each market's requirements.
Coached underperforming annotators back to standard using applied linguistics and instructional design rather than escalation.
Drove measurable improvement against client-defined goals across languages and distributed teams through repeated shifts in priority.

experience.title: Language Specialist & Quality SME — LLM Workflows

highlights.text: Shaped initial project design around client goals and kept living documentation current as those goals moved.
Audited output daily to identify trends, and translated client feedback into concrete guidance the team could act on.
Evaluated and corrected model output to raise response quality, and interpreted ambiguous guidelines for the wider trainer pool.
Researched and verified factual claims in model output, then circulated the findings across a distributed team.
Ran linguistic quality control and back-translation review on high-visibility medical documentation, and transcribed patient interviews.
Delivered under GDPR and HIPAA data-protection requirements throughout.
Annotated multimodal content for NLP/NLG projects using an adaptable semantic labelling system, focused on user and bot interactions.
Held high internal consistency rates across a distributed annotation team.
Facilitated research-based sessions on leadership and communication for managers, executives and individual contributors.
Equipped participants with practical tools for navigating organisational friction.
Trained healthcare professionals online and on-site across a heavy travel schedule.
Rewrote the training materials into structured, performance-driven content, shortening time to competence.
Managed stakeholder buy-in through periods of organisational change.
Delivered complex medical translation projects against tight time and budget constraints without relaxing quality thresholds.
Evaluated technical documents and CAT tooling to improve throughput and accuracy.
Trained new hires on working effectively with international vendors.

experience.title: Language Teaching & Curriculum Design

highlights.text: Designed and taught blended curricula and assessment materials across three countries, including Gaokao English preparation in Shenzhen.
Led instructional design workshops on communication in large classrooms, and supported multinational cohorts of teachers through TEFL training.
